clue.text: Outspoken, shocking court

blocks.note: dire means dreadful, appalling
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A judge or witness speaks bluntly, and the courtroom is scandalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone direct says plainly what they think, which is what being outspoken means.

clue.text: Slipping up, gathering after duke's heroic action

indicators.note: after says the slipping word follows the duke's piece, so the duke comes first

blocks.note: D abbreviates duke
erring means making a mistake
a do is a party, a social gathering

explanation.surface: A duke trips up at a party, hardly a brave deed.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in duke, slip, party order: 'after duke's' puts the duke first.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is bold, daring adventure of the swashbuckling kind, so heroic action.

clue.text: Competitive struggle in desert heat

blocks.note: to rat is to desert or betray
a heat is a preliminary race

explanation.surface: Pictures a hard contest under the desert sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' and 'heat' paint a Sahara scene, but desert is a verb and heat a sporting round.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the fierce, exhausting scramble for success in working life.

clue.text: Lady Chatterley, say, may be against position

blocks.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: Someone hostile to D. H. Lawrence's heroine and what she stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Chatterley's first name in Lawrence's novel is Constance, so she is an example of the name.

clue.text: Cronies upset about a storyline

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
about means going around, so the jumbled letters wrap round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of friends falls out over the plot of a film they are writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of a plot, the sequence of events in a film or play.

clue.text: React badly over girl's free hand

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: react rearranged
Blanche is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone overreacts to a girl being given her own way.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Carte blanche is complete freedom to act as one wishes, an idiom equal to a free hand.

clue.text: Floor of drain in need of repair

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plumber notices the base of a drain is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, so figuratively its floor or bottom.

clue.text: Pretty young woman stood up by friend

blocks.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to stand up
bud is short for buddy, a friend

explanation.surface: An attractive young woman is stood up on a date by her friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood up' looks like a broken date but just means got to one's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is a dated term for a pretty girl just reaching young womanhood.

clue.text: Wild animal needing power to make sudden swoop

indicators.note: needing something means lacking it, so the answer is the longer word without that letter

blocks.note: to pounce is to swoop suddenly
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A wild cat must summon strength to leap on its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer needs a P to become the swoop, so the swoop minus P gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a wild cat of Central Asia.

clue.text: Spherical barrel in Capone's gun

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the first item sits within the second

blocks.note: rod is gangster slang for a pistol, apt for Al Capone
a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: Pictures the barrel of the Chicago gangster's tommy gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrel' looks like part of the gun, but it is a cask going inside the gun word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund means round or plump in shape, close to spherical in form.

clue.text: Exploits lad rated silly, at first

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: rated rearranged
a lad is a boy, a son

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of a boy who was first judged foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' tells you the jumbled word comes before the lad, so it leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade on something is to take unfair advantage of it, a verb matching exploits.

clue.text: Comic bare for short comedy play

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word that follows loses its last letter
comic suggests clowning about, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
comedy cut short

explanation.surface: Reads like a review: a naked comic turn makes for a brief comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedroom Farce is a 1975 comedy by the English playwright Alan Ayckbourn.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayckbourn's Bedroom Farce is a stage comedy, so it is an example of a play.

clue.text: I haven't, by inference, being a Russian leader

definitions.text: I haven't, by inference, being a Russian leader

blocks.note: surface reading: a speaker denying something they have done

blocks.clueFragment: by inference, being a Russian leader
blocks.note: setter's reading: drop the h as careless speakers do and the words run together into a tsar's name, spoken terribly

explanation.surface: Someone protests their innocence, and is taken to be a Russian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the H, 'I haven't' comes out as 'I 'aven't', roughly 'Ivan T'; we infer the speech is terrible, hence the tsar's epithet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV, the first tsar of all Russia, was nicknamed for his cruelty in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Fresh information about being imprisoned

indicators.note: something imprisoned is locked inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: New reports have come in about someone being jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means new, unripe or inexperienced, so it can stand for fresh.

clue.text: Character on form, one worthy of imitation

blocks.note: an actor plays a character, a role
a form or pattern to copy is a model

explanation.surface: Reads like praise for a person of good character who is on form.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person others look up to and copy in behaviour.

clue.text: Mine eager, working in zoo

indicators.note: working means in operation and moving about, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A keen zookeeper is hard at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for exhibition, a small zoo.

clue.text: Dealing with one may generate a lot of interest

definitions.text: Dealing with one may generate a lot of interest

blocks.clueFragment: Dealing with one may generate a lot of interest
blocks.note: surface reading: a fascinating person who attracts curiosity
setter's reading: interest as the charge on borrowed money, run up at extortionate rates by an illegal lender

explanation.surface: Meeting a certain person is bound to arouse plenty of curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: Interest is curiosity on the surface but money owed on a loan underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: An extortionate moneylender charges huge interest, so borrowing from one runs up a big debt.

clue.text: Disturbed now and then, about to film

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of order, so the following letters get mixed up
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is upset every so often when about to shoot a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now and then' reads as 'occasionally' but is the letter supply; 'about to' looks like a phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Town is a 1949 MGM musical with Gene Kelly and Frank Sinatra as sailors on leave.

clue.text: City in northern Italy with name of American one

blocks.note: Trento is a city in the Trentino region of northern Italy
N abbreviates name

explanation.surface: An Italian city shares its name with a city in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' leads the clue, but the definition is 'American one', with one meaning a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenton is the state capital of New Jersey in the United States.

clue.text: Girl Irish boy knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned upside down, which in letters means read backwards

blocks.note: Aidan is a traditional Irish boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl knocks down an Irish lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia is a female given name, of Slavic origin, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Daughter Laura raving about chapter in novel

indicators.note: raving means wild and frenzied, so the name's letters are thrown about
about means going round, so the jumble surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: D abbreviates daughter
taken as written, to be rearranged
C abbreviates chapter

explanation.surface: A daughter called Laura rants over a chapter of a book she is reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is Bram Stoker's 1897 Gothic horror novel about the vampire count.

clue.text: Sign on lawn - Don't Smoke Cannabis

blocks.note: first meaning: the notice telling people not to walk on a lawn
second meaning: grass is slang for cannabis, so avoid it

explanation.surface: A park notice that seems to double as an anti-drug warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is a common slang word for marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the usual park notice and also, punningly, advice to steer clear of marijuana.

clue.text: Poet buried in Stoke, at Shelton

indicators.note: buried in means lying inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: A poet lies interred in Shelton, a district of Stoke-on-Trent.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelton is part of Stoke-on-Trent in the English Potteries, which gives the burial a plausible address.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was a major English Romantic poet of the early nineteenth century.

clue.text: Love unaltered fertile spot

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
as is means in its present, unchanged state

explanation.surface: An unchanging love is a place where things grow.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a green area in a desert watered by a spring, so a fertile patch.

clue.text: Stair repaired with effort and great skill

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a try is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: A craftsman fixes a staircase with care and considerable expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill or craftsmanship of a high order.

clue.text: Drawing round university graduate revealing injury

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: drawing is a form of art
U is the abbreviation for university
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A student's artwork exposes the scars of some past hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like it wraps the university, but it turns the drawing word back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is a physical wound or a deep psychological shock, either sense an injury.

clue.text: Knocking back endless wine is ominous

indicators.note: without an end, so the wine's final letter is cut off
knocking back a drink sounds like downing it, but here it means turning the letters backwards

blocks.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine, here missing its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drinking non-stop is a bad sign for the drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' suggests drinking; it reverses the whole run of letters after the Greek wine loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening or suggesting harm to come, as ominous does.

clue.text: Comment about stain

blocks.note: re means concerning
a mark is a stain or blemish

explanation.surface: Someone passes remarks about a stain on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a spoken or written observation, which is a comment.
